tasks.short: Review the record, results and referral, examine and talk with the patient, diagnose and decide treatment, consult physicians and other providers, and document the consultation.

steps.what: Nurse practitioner reviews the record, results and referral
Nurse practitioner examines and talks with the patient
Nurse practitioner diagnoses and treats complex, unstable or comorbid conditions
Nurse practitioner consults physicians and other health care providers
Nurse practitioner documents the consultation in the record

loop.input: The recording of the consultation, made with the patient's consent.
loop.output: A draft SOEP note in the record.
loop.check: A validator flags every medication, dose and diagnosis not confirmed elsewhere in the record; the nurse practitioner reads each draft against the examination and the decisions taken, corrects it, and types the note when the draft misses or changes a finding.
loop.stop: One draft per consultation; if the nurse practitioner rejects it, they write the note.
loop.why_not_simpler: Typing from memory is the work being cut; a template still needs the consultation in prose.

tasks.design: The record ({OTHER}) shows referral, recent results and medication on one screen before the consultation. With the patient's consent, a certified scribe drafts the SOEP note from the recording; a validator flags any medication or diagnosis not found elsewhere, and the nurse practitioner corrects and approves every note. Examining, diagnosing, treating and consulting colleagues stay with the nurse practitioner.
tasks.previous_blocker: Information was spread over several screens and notes were typed after the consultation.
tasks.enabler_now: Certified medical scribes draft notes into Dutch care records.
tasks.still_hard: Complex patients' stories do not fit short notes; drafts can contain errors.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising that an unstable patient needs a physician now.
tasks.altitude: The nurse practitioner checks drafted notes instead of typing them.

reach.learn: Whether notes are complete when consulted.

evidence.claim: Tandem's scribe and coding carry MDR class IIa.
At Capio Ramsay Santé, 1,295 clinicians using Tandem notes self-estimated time per note falling from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes.
The IGJ holds providers responsible for careful use of generative AI, including testing and monitoring after updates.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient referral to the consultation note; follow-up appointments are outside.
Input contract: recordings only with consent; fallback is typing the note.
Examining, diagnosing and consulting do not change.
A DPIA and processor agreement come before recording.
s1 keeps 75: reading stays; opening several tabs goes. s5 keeps 70, near the 29% per-note cut seen in scribe cases, because every note is read and corrected.
research_questions: How often does the validator flag an unconfirmed medication?

already_counted.description: Nurse practitioner reads and corrects drafted notes.

incremental.description: Nurse practitioner asks consent for recording.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of patients decline recording, so s5 keeps 85, and the summary screen misses outside results, so s1 keeps 90 (2.7); high: most consultations recorded (7.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Look up dosing for the patient's age, weight and kidney function, decide drug, dose, route and frequency, write the prescription, check interaction and contraindication alerts, and send the prescription to the pharmacy.

steps.what: Nurse practitioner looks up dosing based on patient characteristics such as age and weight
Nurse practitioner decides medication dosages, routes and frequencies
Nurse practitioner writes the prescription
Nurse practitioner checks the final prescription: drug, dose, route and frequency match the decision, alerts are resolved, and it goes to the patient's pharmacy
Nurse practitioner sends the checked prescription: printed for the patient today, sent electronically to the patient's pharmacy after the change

tasks.design: The prescribing module ({OTHER}) computes dose options from age, weight and kidney function in the record and runs rule-based checks for interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates, so the nurse practitioner does not look up tables. Order sets fill route and frequency for common treatments. The nurse practitioner decides and checks every prescription; the nurse practitioner releases each checked prescription to the patient's pharmacy electronically. No software prescribes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Doses were looked up in references and prescriptions printed or phoned.
tasks.enabler_now: Prescribing modules compute doses from record data and check them by rule.
tasks.still_hard: Too many alerts lead to alert fatigue.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a lower dose for a frail patient the rules call average.
tasks.altitude: The nurse practitioner decides and checks instead of looking up and copying.

reach.learn: Whether fewer prescriptions need a callback.

evidence.claim: The G-Standaard checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates; KNMP sets the content.
A prescription comes from a named practitioner; software drafts and checks but does not prescribe.

assumptions: Boundary: from the treatment decision to the prescription sent; dispensing is outside.
Input contract: weight and kidney function in the record; fallback is reference tables.
Deciding the dose stays with the nurse practitioner.
The pharmacy receives e-prescriptions.
s1 keeps 30 for reading the computed options; s3 keeps 60 because order sets cover common treatments only; s5 keeps 10 for the release.

incremental.description: Nurse practitioner reports irrelevant alerts for tuning.

approvals.approved_version: The prescription with drug, dose, route and frequency exactly as checked by the nurse practitioner in s4, sent once electronically to the patient's pharmacy; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: weight or kidney function is often missing, so dosing is still looked up (s1 keeps 70), and order sets fit few prescriptions (s3 keeps 80) (20.0); high: complete data and order sets for most (34.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review home measurements and lab results, consult the patient, adjust treatment for chronic problems such as high blood pressure and diabetes, document the care plan, and schedule the next check-up and tests.

steps.what: Nurse practitioner reviews the patient's paper log of home measurements and lab results
Nurse practitioner consults the patient about the chronic condition
Nurse practitioner diagnoses and treats chronic health care problems such as high blood pressure and diabetes
Nurse practitioner documents the consultation and care plan
Nurse practitioner plans the next check-up and lab tests: by hand today; after the change a recall rule proposes them from the care plan
Nurse practitioner checks the proposed check-up date and lab request: they fit the adjusted treatment, and the request goes to the right lab
Nurse practitioner releases the checked recall and lab request

tasks.design: Home blood pressure and glucose readings sync from patients' connected devices into the record ({OTHER}) and show as a trend beside lab results, so the nurse practitioner does not read paper logs. The chronic care template has standard fields per condition. A recall rule proposes the next check-up and lab request from the care plan, which the nurse practitioner checks and releases. Consulting the patient and adjusting treatment stay with the nurse practitioner.
tasks.previous_blocker: Patients brought paper logs and follow-ups were planned by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Home devices sync readings to records; recall rules plan follow-up.
tasks.still_hard: Not every patient has a connected device.
tasks.human_edge: Finding out why a patient stopped taking their pills.

evidence.claim: Connected home devices can sync blood pressure and glucose readings to care records.
Health data are special category data; expect a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: from the check-up due to the follow-up planned; specialist referral is outside.
Input contract: patients with connected devices; fallback is paper logs.
Patients' devices sync without extra steps; no added patient time.
Consulting and adjusting treatment do not change.

s1 keeps 50 for reading the trend view. s4 keeps 80: standard fields save some typing, but the care plan is the nurse practitioner's own record. s5 keeps 40 for reading the proposal; its check (s5b) and release (s5c) take 1 each.
research_questions: Do more patients reach their blood pressure target?

incremental.description: Nurse practitioner helps patients connect their device.

approvals.approved_version: The next check-up date and lab request exactly as checked by the nurse practitioner in s5b, booked once in the agenda and sent once to the lab; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few patients have connected devices, so paper logs stay and s1 keeps 90 (6.3); high: most patients sync readings (14.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check guidelines and the formulary for efficacy, safety and cost, decide the medication within legal authority, explain the choice to the patient, check the final prescription, and send it to the pharmacy.

steps.what: Nurse practitioner checks guidelines and the formulary for efficacy, safety and cost
Nurse practitioner prescribes medications based on efficacy, safety and cost as legally authorized
Nurse practitioner explains the choice to the patient
Nurse practitioner checks the final prescription: drug, dose and instructions match the choice explained to the patient, and it goes to the patient's pharmacy
Nurse practitioner sends the checked prescription: phoned to the pharmacy today, sent electronically after the change

tasks.design: The prescribing module ({OTHER}) shows the preferred drugs from the guideline and the insurer's formulary with price and reimbursement status for the diagnosis, so the nurse practitioner does not look them up separately. Weighing options and explaining them to the patient stay with the nurse practitioner, within their legal authority. The nurse practitioner releases each checked prescription to the pharmacy electronically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Guidelines, formularies and prices were looked up in separate sources.
tasks.enabler_now: Prescribing modules show guideline drugs and formulary status.
tasks.still_hard: Cheapest is not always best for the patient.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a drug the patient will actually take.

reach.learn: Whether preferred drugs are prescribed more often.

evidence.claim: The G-Standaard checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates.
A prescription comes from a named practitioner under the Wet BIG; software does not prescribe.

assumptions: Boundary: from the treatment need to the prescription sent; dispensing is outside.
Input contract: formulary data loaded in the prescribing module; fallback is separate look-ups.
Deciding stays with the nurse practitioner within legal authority.
The pharmacy receives e-prescriptions.
s1 keeps 50 for reading the options and weighing them; looking up separate sources goes. s5 keeps 10 for the release.
research_questions: Does the share of preferred drugs rise?

incremental.description: Nurse practitioner reports outdated formulary entries.

approvals.approved_version: The prescription exactly as checked by the nurse practitioner in s4, sent once electronically to the patient's pharmacy; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly repeat prescriptions where formulary look-ups are rare, so s1 keeps 80 (13.5); high: many new prescriptions with formulary checks (21.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The nurse practitioner keeps examining, diagnosing, deciding treatment and prescribing; typed notes, dose look-ups, paper logs and phoned prescriptions shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking drafted notes and alert lists
role.ambitious_version: A nurse practitioner with more time for complex patients.
